title: Macroeconomics Adventure 3: Monetary & Fiscal Policy
welcome_lead: Today you'll compare the central bank's monetary tools with the government's fiscal levers.
meta_desc: Economics Macro: monetary policy (interest rates, QE) and fiscal policy (tax and spend).
final_note: You contrasted monetary and fiscal policy and considered their strengths and limits.

concepts.def: Boosts AD: lower rates or higher G
Cools AD: higher rates or lower G
Quantitative easing — central bank asset buys
Tax / benefit that smooths the cycle

walkthroughs.body_html:
Central banks (ECB, Fed, BoE) target inflation (usually 2%).

Tools: policy interest rate, open market operations, reserve requirements, QE.

Transmission: rate ↓ → borrowing ↑, currency ↓, asset prices ↑ → AD ↑.

Lags: typically 12–18 months. Liquidity trap can render rates ineffective at zero lower bound.

Government varies G and T.

Expansionary: cut T or raise G — boosts AD, may widen deficit.

Contractionary (austerity): raise T or cut G — cools AD, reduces debt.

Automatic stabilisers: progressive tax and unemployment benefits cushion the cycle without legislation.

Monetary: fast, flexible, can be reversed; blunt — affects everyone, may worsen inequality, weak at zero rates.

Fiscal: targeted, can build infrastructure; slow (political), crowds out private investment, raises debt.

Best mix depends on the cycle and on central bank independence.
